registered_before: any positive selection on terrain, any background point, any terrain/land-cover/geology/OSM value, any model fit or score of this version. Only inventory attribute counts (process, position class, project, year) had been looked at (PROJEKTBEWERTUNG_VOR_ZUSAMMENFUEHRUNG.md and this session).
status: pre-registered leave-one-area-out evaluation. The primary endpoint is confirmatory within this design; every secondary analysis is exploratory. Not a sealed test: no area is kept back for later.
question: Does a static model trained on the terrain and geology around precisely located pure Hangmuren of other Austrian areas rank the Hangmuren of a completely held-out area above random background points of that area better than slope alone?
primary_endpoint: SRTM variant, hist_gradient_boosting with feature set terrain_geology: AUC of held-out positives versus held-out background inside each evaluation area (leave-one-area-out), mean over evaluation areas with equal area weights
primary_comparison: paired per-area difference AUC(hgb terrain_geology) - AUC(hgb slope_only), mean over evaluation areas; 95 % percentile interval from the area bootstrap
decision_rule: 'better than slope alone' only if the 95 % interval of the mean paired difference lies entirely above 0; 'above chance' only if the 95 % interval of the mean AUC lies entirely above 0.5; otherwise 'no established benefit'. Results are relative susceptibility rankings, never probabilities of a landslide.
must_not_change: V0.4 registration, freeze and sealed test (reports/v04, config/v04.json)
wirkungskette_v02 registration and results (other session); no results of this version on its areas are sent to it before its test is frozen
comparisons_counted: primary 1; secondary listed under evaluation.secondary (11 analyses); all are reported, including those without a benefit

positives.source: GeoSphere Austria Naturgefahren inventory, local snapshot (retrieved 2026-10-14, 25 609 records)
positives.not_used: 'Hangmure bis Lockergesteinsrutschung', 'Hangmure und Lockergesteinsrutschung' and all other subgroups are counted, never used as positives (mixed process class; AGENTS.md section 17). They do not run separately in v01.
positives.no_other_quality_filter: QUAL_MB and QUAL_PROZ are counted and reported, not filtered
positives.event_year: EREIGNIS_J if present, else the single four-digit year in RegKatE_ID, else unknown
positives.deduplication_rule: greedy in EPSG:31287 metres: sort by (has RegKatE_ID, year known, position class 0-5 m before 5-20 m, OBJECTID) and keep a record only if no kept record lies within 30 m; done once over all candidates before any terrain value
positives.terrain_checks: DEM value finite, 0-4500 m, DEM slope >= 5 deg at the positive cell; otherwise excluded and counted (same minimum as the background)

dem.date_rule: the provenance of the height data must precede the event (user decision 2026-10-18: provenance counts instead of the file date), consistent with wirkungskette_v02

primary.name: srtm
primary.source: SRTM 1 arc-second (SRTMGL1 v3, NASA/USGS, acquisition 11-22 February 2000), ESA STEP mirror https://step.esa.int/auxdata/dem/SRTMGL1/<tile>.SRTMGL1.hgt.zip
primary.limitation: C-band surface model (includes forest canopy and buildings), smoother than a laser terrain model; SRTMGL1 v3 voids are filled from later sources (ASTER GDEM, GMTED), so a small share of cells in steep terrain has later provenance

sensitivity.name: skadi
sensitivity.source: Mapzen/AWS Skadi 1 arc-second composite (the V0.4 tiles; over Austria based on the data.gv.at laser-scan DGM, acquisitions not demonstrably before 2005-2015)
sensitivity.eligible_positives: all positives regardless of year, including unknown years and Thiersee 1970 ('alle Inventardaten')
sensitivity.label: sensitivity analysis: height-data provenance not demonstrably pre-event; never the headline

dem.grid_origin: cell edges at integer multiples of 30 m in EPSG:31287
dem.resampling: bilinear from geographic 1 arc-second, nodata -32768 -> NaN
dem.sample_rule: a point takes the values of the 30 m cell that contains it

areas.project_area: RegKatE_ID (stripped); all its positives form one area
areas.tile_area: positives without RegKatE_ID: fixed 50 km x 50 km tiles in EPSG:31287 with edges at multiples of 50 000 m
areas.evaluation_area: an area with >= 10 included positives in the DEM variant; smaller areas are training-only (always in training, listed and counted)
areas.sampling_region: union of the fixed 5 km x 5 km lattice cells (EPSG:31287, edges at multiples of 5000 m) that contain >= 1 included positive of the area, clipped to Austria. Boundaries come from the fixed lattice, never from the point shapes (no hulls, no buffers around positives)
areas.independence_note: areas are the units of resampling. Same-storm areas (Vorarlberg/Tirol and Gasen/Haslau August 2005; Nordhaelfte and Taxenbach June 2013) are kept separate (different regions) and reported as possibly dependent

background.draw: uniform in the area's sampling region, candidate stream seeded by sha256(area_id, seed); accepted in stream order until 3 x n_positives are found
background.inventory_buffer_rule: no background point within 100 m (EPSG:31287 metres) of ANY inventory record with geometry (all processes, all position classes)
background.shortfall: an area whose region cannot supply the background is excluded and counted
background.label: PSEUDO_NEGATIVE: random slope cell without a documented inventory record nearby, not a confirmed stable slope
background.variant_rule: the same candidate stream per area for both DEM variants; acceptance (slope, elevation) evaluated on the variant's DEM

features.terrain_code: preslide.terrain.derivatives and preslide.v04.terrain (curvatures, disc, focal_mean, fill_depressions, flow_accumulation), unchanged algorithms; catchment/TWI MISSING when the upslope area reaches the window edge
features.aspect: only as sin/cos of the downslope azimuth (circular)

geology.source: GeoSphere Austria INSPIRE GeologicUnit 1:500 000 (CC BY 4.0), whole layer cached
geology.missing: no or several polygons with different lithology at a point = all five indicators MISSING

land_cover.vintage_rule: latest CORINE vintage whose imagery ended before the event year: CLC2000 (imagery 1999-2001) for 2002-2007, CLC2006 (2005-2007) for 2008-2012, CLC2012 (2011-2012) for 2013-2018, CLC2018 (2017-2018) for 2019+
land_cover.area_rule: an area enters the land-cover analysis only if all its included positives have a known year >= 2002 that maps to one vintage; its background takes that vintage
land_cover.missing: no or several polygons at a point = all five indicators MISSING
land_cover.caveat: most positives were mapped on orthophotos ('Ferndiagnose - Orthofoto'): slides under forest canopy are hard to see, so a forest contrast is partly a visibility artefact

features.forbidden: no weather, no coordinates (x, y, lon, lat), no distance to roads/buildings, no distance to or count of other inventory events, no area or project identifier, no event year
features.missing_values: never invented. HistGradientBoosting: native missing handling. Logistic regression: training-median imputation plus one missing indicator per feature with any missing training value; counts reported

models.training_weights: every sample of a training area weighted 1/sqrt(n_positives of that area), so the largest documentation does not dominate
models.no_tuning: no hyperparameter search, no seed search, no feature selection; no neural network

evaluation.scheme: leave-one-area-out over evaluation areas: the held-out area is never in training
evaluation.spatial_purge_rule: for each held-out area, every training sample (any area) within 1000 m of any held-out sample is removed before fitting
metrics_per_area: capture_top20: share of positives scoring above the 80th percentile of the area's background scores (chance 0.20)
evaluation.aggregation: mean over evaluation areas, equal weights (units = areas)
secondary: 1 slope_rule (raw slope) and logistic regression terrain_geology, each with its paired difference to hgb slope_only
2 positive-pooled AUC over all held-out predictions (descriptive)
3 mean over areas without the largest evaluation area
4 capture_top20 and average precision for every model
5 per-area table for every evaluation area (all reported)
6 skadi sensitivity: the whole LOAO on the skadi sample set (all positives)
7 land cover: LOAO restricted to land-cover areas, hgb and lr terrain_geology_landcover vs terrain_geology on the same samples (paired)
8 reporting bias (as V0.7): AUC of -log10(1 + distance to nearest OSM building or public road) per area (distance is never a model feature)
9 reporting bias: primary predictions re-scored only on samples with distance to infrastructure >= 200 m (areas with >= 5 positives and >= 5 background left), paired vs slope_only
10 DEM-date description: SRTM-variant areas with event year >= 2017 (Skadi file also pre-event) listed separately
11 per-feature permutation importance of the primary model on the held-out areas (descriptive, 'the model relied on', not causal)

reporting_bias_control.source: OpenStreetMap via Geofabrik, data/v07/source/austria-261014.osm.pbf (ODbL; sha256 3d00a7f2e50b6338ff91f3c140715b5a7513057896c9d21eda60b7afc7ad01cf, recorded in data/v07/source.json), registered V0.7 definitions (preslide.v07.infrastructure: buildings any 'building' tag except 'no'; public roads incl. service; cap 5000 m)

demo.area_rule: the SRTM-variant evaluation area with the most included positives
demo.block_rule: the 300 x 300 cell processing block of that area containing most of its included positives
demo.model: hgb terrain_geology (srtm) from the leave-one-area-out fold that held out the demo area (the area is NOT in its training)
demo.layer: score of every 30 m cell of the block (slope >= 5 deg, inside Austria, features computable), shown as percentile rank within the block = relative susceptibility; slope-only layer from the same fold for comparison
demo.web_bundle: aggregates and the demo layer; record-level inventory coordinates stay local

pilot: 1 -> 5 -> 20 areas (or all if fewer) with the full chain, checked, then all areas
